content: No, it is not true that Romansh is a fully-fledged official language of Switzerland applicable to all official documents and for all federal authorities. Romansh is indeed one of Switzerland's four national languages and has official status in the Canton of Graubünden, where it is used in official documents and by local authorities. However, at the federal level, Romansh is not used in official documents or by federal authorities. The other three official languages at the federal level are German, French, and Italian.
